page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 192 dedicated physical arm64 cores based on AWS Graviton processor architecture operating at 2.7 GHz. With a single thread per core and no hyperthreading overhead, the server provides full bare-metal access to 192 vCPUs alongside 768 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4 GB RAM per physical core.

The hardware platform features an extensive network subsystem delivering a 600 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated local storage or discrete graphics processing units, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions for data persistence. This architecture targets applications requiring massive parallel processing, extensive network throughput, and consistent core-level execution without hypervisor contention.

From an architectural perspective, the bare-metal allocation model eliminates virtualization penalties and resource contention, delivering predictable CPU throughput across all 192 dedicated arm64 cores. Primary tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and the lack of x86-specific instruction sets. Suitable workloads include large-scale distributed databases, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration and build pipelines, network-intensive microservices, and general-purpose enterprise application serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 192 dedicated physical arm64 cores powered by AWS Graviton processors at a 2.7 GHz clock speed. Each core runs a single thread, delivering direct hardware execution across 192 vCPUs with 768 GB of total system memory, conforming to a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory profile of 4 GB per core. The server includes a high-capacity 600 Gbps baseline network interface to sustain heavy inter-node and network traffic. The m8gn.metal-48xl contains no onboard local storage drives and no dedicated graphics accelerators, depending on external network storage solutions for persistent disk volumes. Because of its bare-metal configuration, it removes hypervisor virtualization overhead, offering consistent processing execution across all cores. This instance is suited for large-scale container platforms, high-throughput network applications, distributed enterprise backend architectures, and intensive memory-to-CPU balanced processing pipelines.
